text:
Bo Horvat is the Islanders' captain and their hardest-matched forward, and his season is a little better than his line. He has nine goals and 21 points in 23 games, on 10.9 expected goals of his own. The goals are behind the chances, which usually means more are coming.

The Islanders take 55% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, 6.0 points better than without him. That is good work for a centre who draws top competition every night. He carries the puck into the zone on 62% of his entries in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, high for a forward, and he still throws his body around (33 hits). Our numbers say he plays like Alex Tuch.

The coverage this month has been about leadership as much as goals: how he handles the room after a bad loss, and what it means to captain a team with Matthew Schaefer growing into a star. Our range projects 60 to 83 points, and 27 to 42 goals.
